A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of PSA tests for cancer‐screening purposes in young men is low, and the rate of use is decreasing.
there is little evidence that PSA screening is used in young men, but that there is evidence that it is used in men at risk of prostate cancer.
there is no evidence that the PSA test is useful for cancer-risk stratification in men younger than age 50 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSA testing in young men is not uncommon and is associated with increased cancer detection.
PSA testing in young men in this study was associated with higher risk of prostate cancer, and that this risk was not associated with PSA testing in older men.
